subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Mars Climate Orbiter
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Mars Climate Orbiter.

hook.text: NASA lost a $125 million Mars probe because one team used metric units and another used imperial. Nobody checked.

buildup.text: In 1999 the Mars Climate Orbiter approached Mars 170 km too close and burned up in the atmosphere.

discovery.text: Lockheed's software sent thrust data in pound-seconds. NASA's code expected newton-seconds. A simple unit mismatch.

twist.text: Engineers noticed trajectory errors weeks earlier but didn't escalate. Organizational communication failed too.

climax.text: The incident led NASA to mandate rigorous interface testing between all contractor systems.

punchline.text: Metric vs. imperial. A $125 million conversion error.

quiz.question: What caused the Mars Climate Orbiter loss?
options: A unit mismatch between metric and imperial
